problems.title: Regional Warehouse Order Fulfillment Latency Spike
problems.problemStatement: Average dispatch turnaround time increased from 14 hours to 48 hours over the past two weeks, resulting in customer service escalations.
problems.currentSituation: Orders are queuing in the staging buffer faster than the picking floor can pack and scan them.
factsAndEvidence: Verified ERP database dispatch logs show 640 orders delayed beyond SLA.
Barcode scanner battery degradations caused 25% station downtime during shift handovers.
Recent software update to Inventory v4 added 3 mandatory verification modals per item.
missingInformation: Exact network latency metrics between handheld scanners and local Wi-Fi access points during peak hours.
assumptionsAndUncertainties: Assumption: Warehouse floor staff headcount is sufficient if software latency is resolved.
Uncertainty: Whether supplier packaging changes contributed to barcode scan retries.
problems.immediateContainmentAction: Reverted scanner software to v3.8 on 30 primary handheld units; brought in 4 temporary scanning stations.

fiveWhys: Why are dispatches delayed? -> Orders spend 2.5x longer at packing verification stations.
Why do packing stations take longer? -> Operators must scan each item barcode 3 times due to redundant modal popups.
Why are redundant popups occurring? -> New software release v4 enabled compliance verification checks by default.
Why was this enabled without staging validation? -> Release pipeline skipped the floor user acceptance test.
Root Cause: Deployment checklist lacked sign-off requirement from warehouse floor lead prior to production push.
contributingFactors: Inadequate floor Wi-Fi signal in Zone C
rootCauseAnalysis.summaryRootCause: Untested ERP client UX changes pushed directly to production without physical workstation testing.

possibleSolutions.name: Hotfix ERP software to streamline scanning flow into a single confirmation beep
possibleSolutions.description: Deploy software patch removing the redundant confirmation dialogues and optimizing caching.
possibleSolutions.advantages: Directly addresses the 2.5x delay; zero physical hardware cost.
possibleSolutions.risks: Low risk if regression tested on staging handhelds first.

possibleSolutions.name: Permanently increase warehouse packing staff by 4 full-time contractors
possibleSolutions.description: Hire additional manual operators to absorb the extra verification burden.
possibleSolutions.disadvantages: High ongoing payroll expenditure ($14,000/mo); masks root software inefficiency.

problems.recommendedSolution: Deploy ERP Hotfix (SOL-1) combined with Wi-Fi repeater relocation in Zone C.
problems.recommendationRationale: Solves the verified root cause at minimal cost and restores the 14-hour SLA sustainably.
problems.actionPlan: 1. Validate hotfix on test handheld (Oct 14). 2. Roll out to production during 22:00 maintenance window. 3. Monitor dispatch queue for 48 hours.
problems.successCriteria: Average dispatch turnaround time returns to under 16 hours within 48 hours of hotfix release.

decisions.title: Migration from Dedicated Staging Servers to On-Demand Ephemeral Environments
decisions.background: Current staging environment costs $5,800/month while standing idle 68% of the time during non-working hours and weekends.
decisions.businessProblemOrOpportunity: Opportunity to trim recurring cloud spend by 60% while speeding up testing pipelines using containerized preview builds.

optionsConsidered.name: On-Demand Ephemeral Container Environments (Recommended)
optionsConsidered.benefits: Reduces monthly cost to ~$1,900; provides fresh isolated test environments for every pull request.
optionsConsidered.tradeOffs: Initial 2-3 minute cold-start spin-up time for first QA tester.

optionsConsidered.name: Keep Existing Fixed VMs with Scheduled Cron Power-Down
optionsConsidered.benefits: Zero changes to existing developer test workflows.
optionsConsidered.tradeOffs: Saves only 35%; shared staging environments still suffer database collision issues between engineers.

decisions.supportingEvidence: Analysis of past 90 days AWS CloudWatch utilization metrics indicated average CPU utilization below 4.2% outside 09:00-18:00.
decisions.assumptions: Engineers tolerate 2-minute container boot time in exchange for isolated PR staging domains.
decisions.recommendedOption: Option 1: Ephemeral Container Environments via Kubernetes autoscaling.
implementationActions: Implement GitHub Actions runner workflow for ephemeral deployments.
Migrate staging secrets to vault manager.
Decommission legacy EC2 staging instances by Oct 31.
decisions.actualOutcome: Approved in executive technical review; phase 1 implementation scheduled for current sprint.

documents.title: Standard Operating Procedure: Production Incident Severity Classification & Escalation
documents.content:
### 1. Purpose
This procedure defines the criteria and response times for classifying and responding to operational and technology incidents.

### 2. Severity Levels
- **Sev-1 (Critical Outage):** Customer-facing disruption impacting core transactions or data privacy. Maximum response time: 15 minutes.
- **Sev-2 (Degraded Operations):** Major feature impairment with available manual workaround. Maximum response time: 60 minutes.
- **Sev-3 (Minor Defect):** Non-blocking glitch or administrative reporting issue. Maximum response time: 1 business day.

### 3. Escalation Chain
1. Primary On-Call Engineer -> 2. Incident Commander (Alex Morgan) -> 3. VP Engineering -> 4. Executive Stakeholders.

documents.title: Lessons Learned: Cloud Database Failover & Replication Drift
documents.content:
### Key Takeaway
Asynchronous database replication across distant cloud regions can accumulate silent replication lag during high write spikes. Always configure strict monitoring on byte lag before executing planned switchovers.
